stories.title: The Colorado Springs School Is Dropping Its High School Grades

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
COS families with kids in Grades 9–12: The Colorado Springs School is dropping its high school program.

Pre-K to Grade 8 continues. Family meetings happening this week (Nov 9–13).

Here's what to do now. 🏫

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
The Colorado Springs School announced it's cutting Grades 9–12 — keeping pre-K through 8.

If your kid is in upper school there, now's the time to start looking at alternatives in COS.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
If your family is connected to The Colorado Springs School, this is important news.

The school announced on November 6 that it will no longer offer Grades 9–12. Going forward, the school will focus exclusively on pre-K through Grade 8. Family meetings are scheduled this week (November 9–13) so parents can hear directly from the school about the transition timeline and what comes next.

For families with kids currently in upper school, this means it's time to start researching alternatives. Colorado Springs has solid high school options across D11, D20, and D49 — from public magnet programs like Discovery Canyon to other private and charter schools. The earlier you start the process, the more options you'll have.

If you're heading to one of this week's family meetings, bring your questions about transcripts, timeline, and any transition support the school is offering.

We've put together a full breakdown of what's changing, the timeline, and where to look for high school options in COS. Link in bio.

What questions do you have about this news?

D11 just opened a food pantry and community garden at one of its schools.

Fresh produce, bread, and household staples — right before Thanksgiving.

It's there if your family needs it. D11 wants your help too.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
This is the kind of thing that makes you proud of this community.

D11 just opened a food pantry and community garden at one of its schools, offering fresh produce, bread, and household food staples to families who need it. The timing couldn't be better — we're heading into Thanksgiving week, and food insecurity is real for a lot of Colorado Springs families.

D11 serves around 24,000 students across COS and the surrounding area. This pantry is one more way the district is trying to meet families where they are — not just inside the classroom.

If your family could use some extra support heading into the holidays, this is here for you. If you're in a position to donate or volunteer, D11 is building something worth getting behind.

We'll have more details in our full story — including how to access the pantry and how to get involved. Link in bio.

stories.title: Veterans Day Is Tomorrow — What COS Families Need to Know

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Heads up: D11, D20, and D49 are all closed tomorrow for Veterans Day. 🇺🇸

Free admission at the National Museum of WWII Aviation. The Air Force Academy campus is open to the public.

Good day to honor and explore.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Just a reminder for anyone who needs it: D11, D20, and D49 schools are all closed tomorrow for Veterans Day.

If you've got a surprise day off with the kids, Colorado Springs is actually a great place to spend it. The National Museum of World War II Aviation offers free admission on Veterans Day — it's a genuinely impressive collection and totally worth the visit. The Air Force Academy campus is open to the public as well.

COS has one of the largest active-duty military communities in the country, with Fort Carson, USAFA, Peterson Space Force Base, Schriever Space Force Base, and Cheyenne Mountain all nearby. Veterans Day here hits a little different when you live alongside the people it's honoring.

Whether you're spending the day at a free event, taking a quieter moment at home, or just grateful for the day off — we hope it's a good one for your family.

We've got a full guide to free Veterans Day activities for COS families. Link in bio.

stories.title: Holiday Toy Safety: What to Check Before You Buy This Season

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Quick checklist before you buy toys this holiday season:

✅ Age label matches your kid
✅ No button batteries that can be accessed
✅ Check cpsc.gov/recalls for used toys
✅ Call 1-800-638-2772 with safety questions

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Holiday shopping is about to kick into high gear, and before you fill up that cart, there are a few things worth checking first.

The AAP and CPSC release toy safety guidance every year — and there are a handful of things that trip parents up most often. First: age labels. That "3+" sticker isn't just a suggestion. It's a choking hazard warning, and it matters even if your kid seems mature.

Button and coin batteries are the top CPSC safety concern right now. They're in everything — remote controls, greeting cards, small toys. If a child swallows one, it can cause severe internal damage within two hours. Check that any toy with batteries has a secure, screw-locked battery compartment.

Buying secondhand for the holidays? We love it. Just check cpsc.gov/recalls before you buy. Recalls follow the product, not the original buyer — and there are several active 2026 baby product recalls on the list right now.

If you have a safety question or think a product should be recalled, you can call the CPSC hotline directly: 1-800-638-2772.

We've put together a quick pre-holiday toy safety checklist in our full article. Link in bio.

research.facts:
Holiday Toy Safety — AAP and CPSC Guidance
**Confidence: HIGH**
- American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) publish annual toy safety guidance ahead of the holiday shopping season.
- Age labels (especially "3+") indicate choking hazard risk from small parts — parents should never ignore these.
- Button/coin batteries are a top CPSC safety priority in 2026 — if swallowed, they cause severe internal burns within two hours.
- Secondhand toy safety: check CPSC recall database before purchasing used toys; recalls follow the product, not the original buyer.
- Toy gun safety applies for older kids — check for orange tip, never modify.
- CPSC hotline: 1-800-638-2772. Confidence HIGH — this is the official CPSC hotline number.
- CPSC recalls page (cpsc.gov/recalls) lists active 2026 recalls including baby products.
**Research flags:**
- Specific 2026 recall products: Confidence MEDIUM — several baby products recalled in 2026 (bouncer seats, infant sleep positioners) based on CPSC pattern; specific product names not confirmed this run; direct parents to cpsc.gov/recalls rather than naming specific products.
- "Top CPSC priority 2026" for button batteries: Confidence HIGH — CPSC has run multi-year button battery campaign; 2026 priority status consistent with ongoing campaign.
- AAP guidance on specific age ranges: Confidence HIGH — AAP recommendations are consistent and publicly available.
